source: read from the spell descriptions in content/spells/spells.json

effects.target: You take the form of a Tiny or Large creature of the vermin type, gaining any of that form's burrow 30 ft., climb 60 ft., fly 60 ft. (good), swim 60 ft., darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, tremorsense 30 ft., scent, blood drain, constrict, grab, lunge, poison, pull, trample or web. A Tiny form gives a +4 size bonus to Dexterity, a -2 penalty to Strength and a +1 natural armour bonus; a Large form gives a +4 size bonus to Strength, a -2 penalty to Dexterity and a +5 natural armour bonus.
saving throws against mind-affecting effects
effects.note: You do not gain full immunity to mind-affecting effects, only this bonus.

vermin-shape-ii.notes: The Tiny and Large ability adjustments are mutually exclusive, so they stay inside the narrative spec; emitting both as ability_mod specs would apply +4 Str and +4 Dex at once. The mind-affecting bonus is untyped in the prose and spans all three saves, so it is a situational_mod rather than a save_mod.

effects.target: The affected weapon (or 50 projectiles) bypasses damage reduction of one type chosen at casting: bludgeoning, cold iron, piercing, silver or slashing. It still inflicts damage of its normal type and its hardness and hit points are unchanged. It can be cast on a natural weapon or unarmed strike.

versatile-weapon.notes: The prose says it functions like greater magic weapon 'except that' it alters physical properties for damage reduction; no enhancement bonus is stated in this description, so none is emitted.

effects.target: Functions as magic vestment, but only on armour or a shield you are wearing or carrying. While anyone else wears or carries it the spell has no effect, and it resumes when you wear or carry it again.

vestment-of-the-champion.notes: Declined to emit magic vestment's enhancement bonus: this description never states the number, and guessing it would be a bonus the engine stacks wrongly.

effects.target: Choose a focused foe within 60 feet that is at least one size category larger than you as a free action when you cast. Switching focus to another foe within 60 feet is a move action; a foe that moves beyond 60 feet is lost as a focus until you move within 60 feet and spend a move action.
Move through your focused foe's threatened area without provoking attacks of opportunity from it.
cmb
effects.note: on all combat maneuver checks made against your focused foe

effects.target: The first successful melee attack you make against your focused foe each round deals an additional 1d6 points of damage.

vex-giant.notes: The 1d6 is narrative rather than a damage spec: it lands only on a later successful melee attack against the focused foe, and the engine rolls and applies a damage spec at resolution, which would fire it at cast time against the wrong creature.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: The target cannot score critical threats. A natural 20 still hits regardless of AC, but the hit is not eligible for a critical confirmation roll. The spell is discharged the first time a threat is foiled this way.

vexing-miscalculation.notes: Corpus duration is 'minutes/level (1) or until discharged'; the per-level term is emitted and the discharge condition is stated in the narrative spec, since the duration shape cannot hold both.

effects.target: You plant a scrying sensor on a creature, object or point in space you touch, and can see and hear it and roughly 10 feet in all directions. The sensor moves with a creature or object that moves. Magically or supernaturally enhanced senses do not work through this sensor.

vicarious-view.notes: Scrying has no home in the effect vocabulary.

effects.target: Perception checks attempted while asleep
effects.note: The target does not take the normal +10 modifier to the DC of Perception checks made while asleep; recorded here as the equivalent bonus on the check.

effects.target: On detecting a threat or unexplained noise while asleep, wake immediately and stand up from your sleeping position as a free action.
If roused and you return to sleep during the duration, you fall asleep immediately and do not count as having your sleep interrupted, even if you fought while awake.

vigilant-rest.notes: The spell removes a +10 penalty to a DC rather than granting a bonus; the situational_mod's note records which direction the prose states, because a situational_mod is narrated to the GM rather than applied by the engine.

effects.target: damage
effects.note: A single melee damage roll; the creature must choose to use the bonus before making the roll. Ranged and spell attacks are unaffected.

vigor.notes: Corpus duration is 'minutes (1) or until discharged'; the discharge is carried by the once-only use limit.

effects.target: will
effects.note: Each dog saves separately. A dog that trusts you (trained by you for a purpose, or in your care at least 30 days and generally well treated) takes a -4 penalty on this save.

on_failure.target: The dog becomes an evil monstrous creature with a hell hound's statistics, except that it has acid, cold and fire resistance 5 instead of fire immunity and cold vulnerability, its bite deals an extra 1d6 points of acid damage rather than fire, and its breath weapon becomes a 10-foot cone of vapour dealing 2d4 points of acid damage. It cannot understand Infernal but understands any language you know, and is neutral evil (lawful evil if you are lawful, chaotic evil if you are chaotic). You command it as you would a creature summoned by a summon monster spell. You can transform one dog per 3 caster levels, to a maximum of five at 15th level. When the duration ends the dogs dissolve into a stinking pile of gore and bones.

vile-dog-transformation.notes: The 1d6 acid bite and the 2d4 cone belong to the transformed dog's own attacks, not to the spell, so they are described rather than emitted as damage. The one-dog-per-3-levels progression counts targets, not dice, so `scaling` is omitted.

effects.target: will
effects.note: Will disbelief. A creature with reason for suspicion that chooses to investigate gets a second save with a +2 bonus as it enters and interacts with the illusion.

on_failure.target: The creature perceives the affected area (one 10-foot cube per caster level) as having suffered a disaster you named at casting and as holding absolutely nothing of interest or worth to it, and moves on without investigating. Creatures with clearly identifiable physical traits you nominate at casting are immune and perceive the area truly. Casting the spell again can extend the area only if you use the same disaster and grant the same creatures immunity; otherwise the entire illusion disappears.

village-veil.notes: Illusion with a per-viewer disbelief save; the vocabulary has no illusion type.

effects.target: One of your natural attacks or unarmed strikes deals an additional 1d6 points of damage, and each creature hit with that weapon must succeed at a Reflex save or be entangled for the spell's duration. A creature that saves is immune to the entangling for 1 round. An entangled creature can spend a standard action to tear the vines off, but further strikes can entangle it again.

vine-strike.notes: Both the 1d6 and the Reflex-or-entangled apply on each later successful strike, not at cast time. A damage spec would roll immediately and a save_gate would resolve the save at casting, so the whole rider stays narrative.

effects.target: ref
effects.note: Success means the vines fail to take root and the spell has no effect.

on_failure.target: land
on_failure.note: Immediate reduction to base speed on the first failed save.

on_failure.target: Each round thereafter the subject must save again or lose another 5 feet of speed, down to half its original speed; the vines can never reduce a creature below 5 feet. As a full-round action the subject or an adjacent creature can tear the vines off, resetting the penalty to 5 feet, though the vines keep growing for the duration. Dealing at least 20 points of fire damage to the subject ends the effect early. Choose one version at casting. Blessed Thorns: at the start of your turn each round the subject takes 2d4 points of damage plus 1 point per round since it last took a full-round action to tear the vines off, and the thorns may be made cold iron or silver for overcoming damage reduction. Noxious Vines: the subject and each adjacent creature must attempt a DC 15 Fortitude save at the start of its turn or be blinded for that round and unable to cast spells with verbal components. Swift Vines: the vines slow the subject 10 feet per round instead of 5, and it becomes staggered once reduced to half speed.

vinetrap.notes: The Blessed Thorns 2d4 repeats every round, so it is narrative — the vocabulary has no repeating-damage type. The escalating speed loss depends on a fresh save each round, so only the first, stated -5 is emitted as a speed spec.

effects.target: The target is cursed to suffer a violent accident at an uncontrolled moment within the next 24 hours. The accident deals 1d8 points of damage per caster level (maximum 5d8) of a type appropriate to its source — fire for an explosion, bludgeoning for a falling object — and the target may attempt a Reflex save when the accident occurs to halve it. Spell resistance can prevent the curse when it is cast; there is no saving throw against being cursed. The accident damages only the target, however much it inconveniences others.

violent-accident.notes: Declined to emit a damage spec despite a stated formula: the damage lands at a GM-chosen moment within 24 hours, not when the spell is cast, and the engine rolls and applies a damage spec at resolution. The damage type is also explicitly variable, so no damage_type would be truthful. Corpus duration is 'days (1) or until discharged'; the discharge is the accident, so until_discharged is the honest kind.

effects.target: will
effects.note: Will negates (object); the firearm, not its wielder, is the target.

on_failure.target: The next time the target firearm fires during the duration it automatically misfires. If the misfire makes the firearm explode, the radius of the explosion is doubled and it deals maximum damage to every creature in the radius. The firearm's wielder also takes 1d6 additional points of fire damage per 2 caster levels (maximum 10d6). If the target is an advanced firearm and it misfires a second time in a row during the duration, it does not explode but still deals the additional damage to the wielder.

violent-misfire.notes: The 1d6-per-2-levels is not the spell's own damage in the engine's sense: it lands on the wielder — a creature other than the target, which is the firearm — and only when the weapon is next fired. Emitted as narrative with the formula intact rather than as a damage spec that would fire at cast time.

effects.target: will
effects.note: Will negates (object), per firearm.

on_failure.target: As violent misfire, except that it affects one firearm per caster level, no two of which can be more than 30 feet apart, at medium range.

violent-misfire-greater.notes: The description is only 'functions as violent misfire except as noted above'; the differences named above it are range and target count, which the corpus already holds. Nothing further is stated, so nothing further is emitted.

effects.target: Every bomb you create and throw during the duration releases up to four vipers on a direct hit: one attacks the creature struck directly and the others attack up to three creatures caught by the splash. The vipers make melee touch attacks using your base attack bonus + Intelligence modifier and deal 1d4 + your Intelligence modifier damage on a hit, and the target is poisoned as if by a venomous snake. The vipers vanish after attacking, hit or miss, and your own bombs do not harm them. This does not interfere with bomb discoveries, but only one bomb admixture can be active at a time — drinking another ends this one.

viper-bomb-admixture.notes: The 1d4 + Int belongs to the conjured vipers' attacks, not to the spell, and only occurs on a later bomb hit; it is not emitted as damage.

virtue.notes: One temporary hit point, stated flatly; no scaling of any kind in the prose.

effects.target: Start a second bardic performance while maintaining another. Starting the second costs 2 rounds of bardic performance instead of 1, and maintaining both costs a total of 3 rounds of bardic performance per round. When the spell ends one performance of your choice ends immediately. This does not stack with any other method of maintaining simultaneous bardic performances.

virtuoso-performance.notes: Purely a permission to hold two performances; no numbers to apply beyond the round costs, which are stated in the permission text.

effects.target: Every living creature in the 40-foot-radius burst centred on you, including you, must immediately attempt a saving throw against every disease it has contracted, even if the onset time has not yet elapsed. On a failed save the affliction has its usual effect; a successful save does not count toward curing the affliction.
the forced saving throw against each contracted disease
effects.note: The -2 applies to the saves this spell forces, not to saves generally.

virulence.notes: The prose says 'a saving throw' without naming which; disease saves are conventionally Fortitude but the spell does not say so, so no save is named and the corpus's own 'see text' stands.

effects.target: Creates fog as fog cloud, except that the vapours carry the taint of disease.
fort
effects.note: A creature that succeeds, or that ignores the fog through spell resistance, is unaffected and makes no further saves even if it stays in the fog.

on_failure.target: saving throws against disease effects
on_failure.note: Applies while the living creature remains within the cloud and for 1d4+1 rounds after it leaves.

virulent-miasma.notes: Only the disease-save penalty allows the Fortitude save and is subject to spell resistance; the fog itself is not, so the fog is a separate narrative spec outside the gate.

effects.target: As legend lore but faster: you pose a question about a person, place or object and receive a vision by succeeding at a caster level check (1d20 + 1 per caster level, maximum +25). The DC is 20 if the person or object is at hand or you are in the place in question; 25 if only detailed information is known, and the vision is incomplete; 30 if only rumours are known, and the vision is vague.
fatigued
effects.note: You are fatigued after the spell completes; this lands on the caster, not on any subject.

vision.notes: Corpus duration is 'see text' and the prose states none, so duration is omitted rather than guessed. The caster level check DCs are quoted in the narrative spec because the vocabulary has no divination type.

effects.target: A realistic illusion of a hellscape overlays the area. Structures, equipment and creatures within it are not hidden, but environmental features take on an infernal appearance. You are prepared for the images and unaffected. Devils and any lawful evil creatures suffer no negative effects.
will
effects.note: Every creature in the area other than you saves; no spell resistance.

on_failure.target: shaken
on_failure.note: Persists as long as the creature remains in the area.

on_failure.target: saving throws against fear effects
on_failure.note: Persists as long as the creature remains in the area.

vision-of-hell.notes: The shaken condition and the -2 both last only while the creature stays inside the area, which the duration shape cannot express, so it is recorded on both specs.

effects.target: Functions exactly as nightmare, and in addition lets a second spell ride along and strike the target the moment it wakes. The second spell must already be prepared and cast immediately after this one, must be 6th level or lower, must affect one target (always the nightmare's recipient) and must not deal hit point damage. Its range is irrelevant, and even touch attacks can be delivered this way, though you must still succeed at the touch attack, the touch occurring within the victim's nightmare. The target may save against the second spell if it normally allows one.

vision-of-lamashtu.notes: Bestow curse, blade barrier, destruction and inflict moderate wounds appear in the prose only as a worked example of what may and may not ride along; none of them is an effect of this spell and none is emitted.

effects.target: Choose one physical ability score at casting. Strength or Dexterity: you gain a +5 bonus on skill checks associated with that ability score. Constitution: your maximum and current hit points increase by an amount equal to your Hit Dice. At any time during the duration you may expend the remaining duration as an immediate action for a one-time enhancement matching your choice, after which the spell ends — Constitution: regain hit points equal to 1d8 + your total character level. Dexterity: gain a +4 dodge bonus to Armor Class for 3 rounds. Strength: gain a +6 bonus on all Strength checks to break objects and on checks to escape or establish grapples for 1 minute.

visualization-of-the-body.notes: Three mutually exclusive branches, each with a standing effect and a different discharge. Emitting them as separate specs would apply all three at once — the +5 skill bonus, the hit point increase, the 1d8 heal, the +4 dodge and the +6 Strength bonus together — so the whole choice tree stays in one narrative spec. Corpus duration is 'hours (24) or until discharged'; the discharge is the immediate action described.

effects.target: ability checks and skill checks associated with the mental ability score you chose
effects.note: Choose Charisma, Intelligence or Wisdom when you cast; the bonus applies to that score's checks only.

effects.target: At any time during the duration you may expend the remaining duration as an immediate action for a one-time enhancement matching your choice, ending the spell. Charisma: a +2 luck bonus on all d20 rolls for 1 minute. Intelligence: a number of ranks equal to your Hit Dice in any one skill in which you have no ranks, for 1 minute, treating it as a class skill for that time. Wisdom: when you fail a Will save you may immediately attempt that save again with a +4 bonus on the new roll.

visualization-of-the-mind.notes: Unlike visualization of the body, the standing +5 is the same whichever mental score you pick, so it is emitted as a real modifier; only the three mutually exclusive discharges stay narrative. The bonus is untyped in the prose. Corpus duration is 'hours (24) or until discharged'.

effects.target: As fire shield, except that yellow or green acidic mist wreathes you instead of hot or cold flames. It deals acid damage to creatures that attack you and protects you against acid damage. It sheds no light.

vitriolic-mist.notes: The damage is retributive — it strikes whoever strikes you, not a target you choose — so it is not emitted as a damage spec. fire shield's own numbers are not restated in this description and are not guessed. The corpus already derives element 'acid'.

effects.target: You alter a humanoid target's voice to anything you choose — high-pitched, husky, nasal, or a different accent you are familiar with. The target can vary the disguised voice just as it could vary its own.
disguise
effects.note: Only when the spell is used as part of a disguise, and only when trying to fool a listener.

vocal-alteration.notes: Not wrapped in a save_gate: the Fortitude save is there for an unwilling target, and gating would make the spell fail to help the willing ally it is normally cast on. The +10 has no stated bonus type.

effects.target: The target gains the ability to speak, understand, read and write one language you choose, excluding secret languages such as Druidic. When you cast the spell you may attempt a DC 15 Linguistics check; on a success choose an additional language, plus one more for every 10 by which the result exceeded the DC. Written material is read at one page (250 words) per minute. As with comprehend languages, this conveys only literal meaning, not insight, and does not allow reading magical writing or deciphering codes. A target without the mental capacity to grasp a language still gains enough to respond to and carry out even extremely complex commands, so instructions to nonsentient creatures must avoid metaphor and ambiguity.

voluminous-vocabulary.notes: Languages have no home in the effect vocabulary.

effects.target: You vomit forth a spider swarm that attacks every other creature in its area. It begins adjacent to you; with no living creature in its area it moves in a direction of your choosing at its normal speed, continuing that way unless you spend a standard action concentrating to move or redirect it. At caster level 7th or higher you may vomit a wasp swarm instead, and at 13th or higher a swarm of army ants.

vomit-swarm.notes: A conjured swarm; its damage is the swarm's, not the spell's. The caster level thresholds change which creature is summoned, not any number the engine rolls, so no scaling.

effects.target: You vomit an ooze copy of yourself into an adjacent square. Whenever you take a move action to move, the twin may move as well; it need not follow you and can take no other action. At the start of your turn on later rounds you may instantaneously exchange places with it as if by teleport — this is not an action and does not provoke attacks of opportunity. The twin has speed 30 feet, provokes attacks of opportunity from movement as normal, has AC equal to 10 + 1/2 your caster level and hit points equal to your caster level. Reduced to 0 hit points it is destroyed, though you may create a new one as a standard action while the duration lasts. You can never have more than one vomit twin at a time.

vomit-twin.notes: The AC and hit point formulas belong to the conjured twin, not to the caster, so they stay described rather than emitted as modifiers to your own sheet.

effects.target: You create a powerful, immobile whirlpool in any body of liquid large enough to contain it.
ref
effects.note: Any Large or smaller creature that comes in contact with the whirlpool saves.

effects.target: A Medium or smaller creature that fails that first save must succeed at a second or be pulled into the whirlpool and held suspended in its currents, taking 1d8 points of damage each round on your turn with no save allowed. You may direct the whirlpool to eject any creature it carries whenever you wish. A boat equal in length to the vortex's width or shorter that passes through takes 6d6 points of damage and is caught up by the current; if its captain succeeds at a DC 25 Profession (sailor) check, or the boat is longer than the vortex is wide, it takes half damage and is not caught.

vortex.notes: Only the 3d6 on contact is emitted as damage — that is one hit on the creature that touched it, the same shape blade barrier and spike growth already use. The 1d8 repeats every round with no save and the 6d6 lands on a boat, so both stay narrative. The prose states no per-level progression, so no scaling.

effects.target: The targets become light enough to be carried by wind. Each takes cumulative penalties for attacking as if under levitate unless it has a fly speed, and is treated as two size categories lighter for being checked or blown away by wind. A target with a fly speed can fly overland at the wind's speed and in the wind's direction by succeeding at a DC 20 Fly check, but risks being blown away as usual if it tries to change direction. By linking hands or joining with rope, affected creatures can be towed through the air by a flying creature as if each weighed one-eighth its actual weight.

waft.notes: Not gated on the Will save: the spell is a mixed blessing cast on allies as often as enemies, and the corpus already records 'Will negates'. The levitate attack penalty is cumulative and not quantified here, so no combat_mod is emitted.

effects.target: fort
effects.note: Fortitude negates. You are never affected by your own wail; creatures closest to the point of origin are affected first.

on_failure.target: The creature takes 10 points of damage per caster level. The spell affects up to one creature per caster level within the 40-foot-radius spread.

wail-of-the-banshee.notes: VOCABULARY GAP: the damage is flat 10 points per caster level with no die, and the scaling schema requires a `die` — scaling_dice() returns nothing without one, and there is no dieless per-level form. Emitting `dice: "10"` would deal 10 points at every caster level, wrong at every level above 1st, so the formula is stated in a narrative spec instead. Duration omitted: the corpus says instantaneous, which the shape supports, but the damage is the whole spell and needs no timing.

effects.target: You and your mount lay a trail of glowing heavenly mist behind you: a path 10 feet wide and up to 120 feet long, floating up to a foot above the ground, running from where you cast the spell to where your mount ends its movement, and persisting 1 round per level thereafter. Good creatures may walk along the top of the mist as if it were solid and treat difficult terrain containing it as normal terrain; evil creatures find it thick and cloying and treat normal terrain containing it as difficult terrain; neutral creatures are unaffected. It does not affect obstacles or impassable terrain, block sight or give concealment. Mounts use their rider's alignment unless they are celestial or fiendish. You must stay mounted — dismounting, being knocked off or otherwise separating from your mount ends the spell, though the mist remains for its normal duration. The wake cannot follow across water, underwater, or through the air.

wake-of-light.notes: Terrain modification has no home in the effect vocabulary; the effect is on squares, not on creatures' sheets.

effects.target: As create pit, except that all but the top 10 feet of the hole is filled with saltwater. Fall damage for anyone falling in is reduced to 1d3 points of nonlethal damage, and Huge or larger creatures at the water's surface can pull themselves out as part of a normal move action with no Climb check. The pit holds one advanced shark per 4 caster levels, to a maximum of four; at casting you may substitute two of those sharks for one great white shark. The sharks immediately attack any creature that falls into the pit, including you, and attack randomly if several fall in. When the spell ends, creatures inside rise up with the bottom of the pit as normal for create pit, but the water and sharks vanish.

walk-the-plank.notes: The 1d3 nonlethal is fall damage taken by whoever later falls in, and the sharks' attacks are the sharks'; neither is emitted as the spell's damage. Corpus duration is 'rounds (1) + rounds/level (1)' — the shape cannot hold a fixed term plus a per-level term, so the per-level term is emitted and the extra round is recorded here.

effects.target: Teleport up to 30 feet as a move action, ending in an unoccupied space you can stand on within line of sight; or spend a move action to teleport from lying prone to standing. This teleporting does not provoke attacks of opportunity.

walk-through-space.notes: A repeatable teleport permission rather than a one-shot movement, so it is a permission spec held for the duration.

effects.target: A translucent wall of energy showing indistinct faces with their eyes or ears sewn shut. Decide when you create it whether it blinds or deafens. It must be vertical and either rectangular or a ring, need not touch the ground, and must be continuous and unbroken when formed; if its surface is broken by any object or creature as it is cast, the spell fails.
fort
effects.note: Any creature that passes through the wall saves.

on_failure.target: The creature is permanently blinded or permanently deafened — whichever you chose when you created the wall — as blindness/deafness.

wall-of-blindness-deafness.notes: Blinded and deafened are mutually exclusive here, chosen at creation, so emitting both apply_condition specs would inflict both at once; the choice stays in a narrative spec inside the gate. Corpus duration is 'concentration + rounds/level (1)' — the duration shape cannot hold a concentration term plus a per-level term, so the per-level term is emitted.

effects.target: A vertical wall of skeletal arms attached to a solid surface, working as wall of stone except as noted. It is 1 inch thick per 4 caster levels, up to one 5-foot square per level, must be vertical and rest on a firm foundation, and cannot bridge a chasm or act as a ramp. Each 5-foot square has hardness 4 and 7 hit points per inch of thickness; a section reduced to 0 hit points is breached, and breaking through with a single attack is a Strength check against DC 15 + 2 per inch of thickness. The skeletal hands attempt a combat maneuver check to grapple each adjacent creature, without provoking attacks of opportunity, at the start of your turn, when the wall is summoned, and when an enemy first moves adjacent. Their CMB equals your caster level and they grapple a Huge or smaller creature without penalty; their CMD for escaping is 10 + that CMB. A foe the wall grapples takes 1d6 points of damage and gains the grappled condition, and takes another 1d6 each round the wall succeeds at a further grapple check. Grappled opponents cannot move until they break the grapple. The wall cannot move or pin foes.

wall-of-bone.notes: The 1d6 comes from the wall's own grapple check and repeats each round it succeeds — a granted attack that repeats, on both counts not the spell's own damage, so it is not emitted as a damage spec.

effects.target: A 5-foot-thick wall of seawater with a powerful current flowing toward one side that you select. Swimming against the current costs 4 squares of movement to enter a square of the wall, and a creature that begins its turn in the wall is ejected in the current's direction just before it acts. The wall gives cover against attacks from out of the water as a body of water usually does, and the water and currents deflect physical ranged attacks into or through it unless the weapon is exceptionally massive, such as a siege engine. A creature submerged in the wall takes the usual penalties for underwater combat. The wall blocks gases and liquids and stops water mixing at its edges.

wall-of-brine.notes: No damage and no save. Corpus duration is 'concentration + rounds/level (1)'; only the per-level term is representable.

effects.target: An immobile vertical wall of spinning cogs and gears, always a flat plane though you may shape its edges to the available space, which cannot be conjured into the space of a creature or object. It gives cover (+4 to AC, +2 on Reflex saves) against attacks made through it. It is 1 inch thick per 4 caster levels, and you may double its area by halving its thickness. Each 5-foot square has hardness 9 and 30 hit points per inch of thickness; a section at 0 hit points is breached, and breaking through with one attack is a Strength check against DC 25 + 2 per inch of thickness. An attacker who rolls a natural 20 — only a natural 20, whatever the weapon's threat range — and confirms the critical gives that section the broken condition, or destroys it if it was already broken. The bronze this spell creates cannot be used to make other objects, even briefly, and cannot be sold.
ref
effects.note: Any creature passing through the wall; a successful save halves the damage.

on_failure.note: The prose says piercing and slashing damage; the damage_type vocabulary holds one type, so piercing is recorded and the slashing half is noted here.

wall-of-clockwork.notes: VOCABULARY GAP: the damage is 'piercing and slashing' — two types at once, which damage_type cannot express. Recorded as piercing rather than untyped, because untyped would silently ignore damage reduction that the real damage is subject to. The 1d6 per 2 caster levels, maximum 10d6, is a stated progression and goes in scaling.

effects.target: A massive veil of ectoplasm roiling with restless spirits, immovable once formed, 1 inch thick per caster level and covering up to one 10-foot square per caster level in any combination of length and height. It may be oriented any way and need not be anchored, but must be created continuous and unbroken, and cannot include squares holding creatures, even creatures on the Ethereal Plane. It exists on both the Material and Ethereal Planes and blocks ethereal and incorporeal creatures. Each 10-foot square has 2 hit points per inch of thickness; a section at 0 hit points is breached, but the remaining ectoplasm immediately fills the hole, shrinking the wall by one 10-foot square while staying contiguous. It can instead take the form of a sphere or hemisphere with a maximum radius of 1 foot per caster level, equally hard to break.
will
effects.note: One side of the wall that you select radiates a mind-affecting fear aura 10 feet from its surface. Creatures in range when the wall is created, or that later approach within 10 feet, must save.

on_failure.target: The creature becomes shaken — or panicked instead if it has 4 Hit Dice or fewer — for 1 round per your caster level.

wall-of-ectoplasm.notes: Shaken and panicked are chosen by the victim's Hit Dice, so an apply_condition spec would inflict the wrong one on low-Hit-Dice creatures; the branch stays narrative. The fear effect's own duration (1 round/caster level) differs from the wall's (1 minute/level), and only the wall's is emitted as the spell duration.

effects.note: Taken by any creature passing through the wall, and by any creature the wall is evoked on top of. Double against undead.

effects.target: One side of the wall, selected by you, sends forth waves of heat dealing 2d4 points of fire damage to creatures within 10 feet and 1d4 points of fire damage to those past 10 feet but within 20 feet. It deals this heat damage when it appears and again to every creature in the area on your turn each round. All of this spell's damage is doubled against undead. If any 5-foot length of wall takes 20 or more points of cold damage in 1 round that length goes away, and cold damage is not halved as it normally is against objects. Wall of fire can be made permanent with permanency; a permanent wall extinguished by cold goes inactive for 10 minutes, then reforms at full strength.

wall-of-fire.notes: The pass-through damage (2d6 + 1 per caster level, maximum +20) is emitted because the prose states outright that creatures the wall is evoked on top of take it as if passing through — so it does land at resolution, on the creature at the wall, with no save. The 2d4/1d4 heat repeats every round on your turn, which the vocabulary has no type for, so it stays narrative. Corpus duration is 'concentration + rounds/level (1)'; the shape cannot hold both terms and the concentration prefix is the load-bearing half of a wall you sustain, so duration is omitted rather than emitted as half a truth. The corpus already derives element 'fire'.

effects.target: An invisible, immobile wall of pure force, formed as a flat vertical plane of up to one 10-foot square per level, continuous and unbroken when formed — if its surface is broken by any object or creature the spell fails. It has hardness 30 and 20 hit points per caster level. It is immune to dispel magic though a mage's disjunction dispels it, is automatically destroyed by disintegrate or by contact with a sphere of annihilation or rod of cancellation, and can otherwise be damaged by spells, weapons and supernatural abilities. Breath weapons and spells cannot pass through it in either direction, though dimension door, teleport and similar effects bypass it and gaze attacks operate through it. It blocks ethereal creatures as well as material ones, though ethereal creatures can usually go around it through material floors and ceilings. It can be made permanent with permanency.

wall-of-force.notes: A barrier with no effect on any creature's sheet; the vocabulary has no type for created structures. The corpus already derives element 'force'.

effects.target: An immobile, blinding curtain of white light that blocks line of sight and sheds bright light 60 feet in all directions. It can be made permanent with permanency, at a minimum caster level of 13th and a cost of 11,000 gp.
fort
effects.note: A creature adjacent to the wall may close its eyes or succeed at this save to negate the blindness for 1 round. A creature that passes through the wall is automatically blinded even with its eyes closed, with no save.

on_failure.target: blinded
on_failure.note: Lasts as long as the creature remains adjacent to the wall, plus 1d4 rounds after it leaves.

effects.target: A creature from the Plane of Shadow gains 1d4 negative levels for each round it spends within 5 feet of the wall (Fortitude negates), and passing through the wall imposes a -4 penalty on that save for that round. Twenty-four hours after gaining them the subject attempts a new Fortitude save for each negative level; each success removes one, and each failure makes that negative level permanent.

wall-of-light.notes: VOCABULARY GAP: negative levels (energy drain) have no effect type — ability_drain only takes an ability score — so the Plane of Shadow clause is narrative. It also only affects one narrow kind of creature, so it would be wrong to apply it from a gate that every creature rolls.

effects.target: A stationary vertical wall of misty vapour, straight, 1 foot thick and up to 10 feet long per caster level. It obscures vision, granting concealment (20% miss chance) against creatures on the other side; a creature sharing a square with the wall counts as on neither side and neither gains nor suffers from that concealment. You may instead create a denser wall, halving its maximum length to 5 feet per caster level: the denser wall also hinders movement, and any creature moving into or trying to pass through it must succeed at a DC 15 Strength check or be entangled and unable to move until the start of its next turn. A creature that starts its turn in the wall can move freely within it or out of either side. Only a severe or stronger wind (31+ mph) disperses the wall, and takes 1 round to do it.

wall-of-mist.notes: The entangling is gated on a Strength check made when a creature later enters the wall, not on a save at casting, so it is not emitted as an apply_condition. Miss-chance concealment has no effect type.

effects.target: A transparent shimmering wall that makes creatures and objects seen through it appear wildly distorted, granting partial concealment (20% miss chance) against creatures on the other side. It must be vertical and rectangular, need not touch the ground, and must be continuous and unbroken when formed; if its surface is broken by any object or creature when it is cast, the spell fails.
fort
effects.note: Any creature that passes through the wall is assailed by overwhelming vertigo and saves.

on_failure.target: nauseated
A creature nauseated this way must also succeed at a DC 12 Acrobatics check or fall prone.

wall-of-nausea.notes: The corpus save field reads 'see text'; the text names Fortitude plainly, so the gate uses it. The prone is a second, conditional check after the nausea lands, so it is not emitted as a second apply_condition.

effects.target: An immobile curtain of illumination. One side, designated by you, radiates bright light 60 feet from that side while the other radiates darkness an equal distance, altering the illumination level by up to two steps toward bright light on the light side or toward darkness on the dark side. The wall obstructs vision through it from either side.

wall-of-split-illumination.notes: Illumination levels have no effect type and the wall touches no creature's sheet.

effects.target: Creates a wall of rock that merges into adjoining rock surfaces, 1 inch thick per four caster levels and up to one 5-foot square per level; you may double its area by halving its thickness. It cannot occupy the space of a creature or object. It may take almost any shape and need not be vertical or rest on a firm foundation, but must merge with and be solidly supported by existing stone, so it can bridge a chasm or serve as a ramp — a span of more than 20 feet must be arched and buttressed, halving the area, and crenellations or battlements cost area likewise. Each 5-foot square has hardness 8 and 15 hit points per inch of thickness; a section at 0 hit points is breached, and breaking through with a single attack is a Strength check against DC 20 + 2 per inch of thickness. It can be destroyed by disintegrate or by ordinary breaking and chipping. Mobile opponents can be trapped within or under the wall if it is shaped to hold them, but they avoid entrapment with a successful Reflex save.

wall-of-stone.notes: A created structure; the Reflex save avoids entrapment rather than an effect the vocabulary can name, so no save_gate is emitted.

effects.target: A wall of glittering motes with no substance that does not obstruct movement but suppresses magic. Any magic item, spell or magical effect of your caster level or lower that passes through it is suppressed for 1 round per level; durations continue to expire while suppressed, and an effect that outlasts the suppression resumes normally. It affects spells, spell-like abilities, magic items and anything stemming from them. It does not suppress a creature's ability to cast spells or use spell-like or limited-use abilities, but a creature with constant or always-active magical abilities that passes through has those suppressed for the normal duration. The wall blocks line of effect, so no spell or effect can pass through it, but it does not block line of sight. Magic items and spell effects of higher caster level than yours are unaffected, as are artifacts, anything stemming from the direct action of a deity, and similarly powerful magic.

wall-of-suppression.notes: suppress_condition covers conditions only, not spells and magic items, so suppression of magic has no effect type.

effects.target: A barrier of tough, pliable, tangled brush bearing finger-length thorns. Any creature forced into the wall or trying to move through it takes piercing damage per round of movement equal to 25 minus the creature's AC, ignoring Dexterity and dodge bonuses to AC — a creature whose AC is 25 or higher without those bonuses takes no damage from contact. Any creature within the area when the wall is cast takes that damage as if it had moved into the wall and is caught inside. A creature can force its way through slowly with a Strength check as a full-round action, moving 5 feet for every 5 points by which the check exceeds 20, up to its normal land speed, taking the damage as it goes; a creature trapped in the thorns can stay motionless to take no further damage. You may make the wall as thin as 5 feet, shaping it as a number of 10-by-10-by-5-foot blocks equal to twice your caster level — this does not change the damage but shortens the time to force through. Creatures able to pass through overgrown areas unhindered cross at normal speed without damage. Edged weapons cut a safe passage 1 foot deep per 10 minutes of work. Normal fire cannot harm the barrier; magical fire burns it away in 10 minutes.

wall-of-thorns.notes: VOCABULARY GAP: the damage is '25 minus the creature's AC', computed from the victim's own defences rather than rolled, and the dice field has no way to say that. It also repeats per round of movement. Both reasons keep it narrative.

effects.target: Sparkling motes of bright light swirl around the target in a complex pattern, clearly outlining it and radiating light as a sunrod, which negates any concealment the target has. The spell affects only enemies; your allies are never affected.
will

on_failure.target: dazed
The target must save again on its next turn or be dazed for another round, and keeps saving each round while the motes stay on it.

on_success.target: The motes jump to the nearest enemy within 30 feet, who then saves each round or is dazed in turn. A creature that has once saved against the motes can never be affected by them again, and if no new target is within 30 feet of a creature that saves, the spell immediately ends.

wandering-star-motes.notes: The first Will save happens when the spell is cast, so the gate is correct here; the repeated saves and the jump to a new victim are described rather than emitted, since nothing in the vocabulary re-targets a spell.

effects.target: The trail left by the targets automatically reroutes, taking any course you choose within the area, and can be made at least half or up to twice its original length. A trail continuing beyond the spell's range must be left connected at that point on the edge of the range. A tracker who beats the DC of the check to follow the trail by an amount equal to your caster level recognises that the trail has been manipulated by magic, but cannot see its true course without magical means such as true seeing.

wandering-trail.notes: Alters tracks in the world rather than any creature; nothing in the vocabulary addresses it.

effects.target: Functions as control weather, except that you may choose to have the weather remain centred on you as you move.

wandering-weather.notes: VOCABULARY GAP: the corpus duration is 'hours (4d12) (see text)' — a rolled duration. The duration shape takes an integer amount, so 4d12 hours cannot be written; duration is omitted rather than guessed at a fixed number.

effects.target: Choose one of four effects at casting; you may change which one as a standard action that reduces the total remaining duration by 1 hour. Spring: light vines and a crown of flowers — the target is immune to bleed effects and regains 1 hit point per round whenever it is below 0 hit points and still alive, which stabilizes it, each hit point restored costing 1 hour of the spell's remaining duration. Summer: motes of light — the target's base speed increases by 10 feet, or it may instead increase its base speed by 30 feet for 1 round at a cost of 1 hour of remaining duration. Fall: a cloak of autumn leaves — the target gains a +2 morale bonus on Fortitude saves, and may roll twice and take the higher result on any save against disease or poison at a cost of 1 hour of remaining duration. Winter: snow and crisp air — the target automatically succeeds at Acrobatics checks to avoid falling while moving across slick or narrow surfaces, and may move freely through difficult terrain for 1 round at a cost of 1 hour of remaining duration, though magically created difficult terrain still affects it normally.

ward-of-the-season.notes: Four mutually exclusive seasons, switchable mid-spell. Emitting them as specs would give the target bleed immunity, +10 speed and a +2 morale bonus on Fortitude saves simultaneously, so the whole choice stays in one narrative spec.

effects.target: The shield grants its wielder spell resistance 10 + your caster level against spells, so long as the shield can be interposed between the wielder and the spell effect. It gives no spell resistance against area spells such as fireball.
ref
effects.note: Against area effect spells, which the shield's spell resistance does not stop.

ward-shield.notes: VOCABULARY GAP: there is no effect type that grants spell resistance to a creature — combat_mod's 'spell_resistance' target is the caster's check to overcome someone else's SR, the opposite direction — so SR 10 + caster level is narrative. The +5 on Reflex saves has no stated bonus type.

effects.target: ac
effects.note: Only for creatures in the emanation who worship the same god, or share the faith, as you. Increases to +3 at caster level 12th and +4 at 18th.

effects.target: fort
effects.note: Increases to +3 at caster level 12th and +4 at 18th.

effects.target: ref
effects.note: Increases to +3 at caster level 12th and +4 at 18th.

effects.target: will
effects.note: Increases to +3 at caster level 12th and +4 at 18th.

effects.target: If you worship no specific deity the bonuses apply to those who share your faith, and if you have no specific faith or religion the spell benefits only you. Enemies who worship your god or share your faith gain the benefits too, however heretical you consider them.

ward-the-faithful.notes: VOCABULARY GAP: the bonus grows from +2 to +3 at 12th level and +4 at 18th, and `scaling` only describes damage and healing dice — there is no way to scale a modifier by caster level. The base +2 is emitted, correct up to 11th level, with the progression recorded on every spec's note.

effects.target: The focus weapon flies above your head and takes a defensive position within your space, lunging at opponents as if martially trained, parrying and turning back melee attacks aimed at you. It never strikes back and deals no damage; it defends only.

Cast spells without provoking attacks of opportunity and without needing to cast defensively. A creature with the Disruptive feat bypasses this: you provoke attacks of opportunity for casting against such creatures even while warded, though you may still choose to cast defensively.

warding-weapon.notes: The prose says outright that the weapon does not strike back and deals no damage, so there is nothing here to convert as damage.

effects.target: Metal bends and warps, permanently destroying its straightness, form and strength. A warped door springs open, or becomes stuck and needs a successful Strength check to open, at your option; a vehicle grinds to a halt and stops working; warped ranged weapons are useless; a warped melee weapon imposes a -4 penalty on attack rolls. You warp one Small or smaller object per caster level, a Medium object counting as two Small, a Large as four, a Huge as eight, a Gargantuan as 16 and a Colossal as 32. You may instead unwarp metal, warping it back to normal; make whole does nothing to repair a warped item. Consecutive castings can be combined to warp or unwarp an object too large for one casting, and the object suffers no ill effects until it is completely warped.

warp-metal.notes: The -4 is a property of the ruined weapon, carried by whoever later wields it, not a modifier this spell places on a creature, so it is not emitted as a combat_mod.

effects.target: Wood bends and warps, permanently destroying its straightness, form and strength. A warped door springs open, or becomes stuck and needs a Strength check to open, at your option; a boat or ship springs a leak; warped ranged weapons are useless; a warped melee weapon causes a -4 penalty on attack rolls. You warp one Small or smaller object per caster level, a Medium object counting as two Small, a Large as four, a Huge as eight, a Gargantuan as 16 and a Colossal as 32. You may instead unwarp wood, warping it back to normal; make whole does no good in repairing a warped item. Consecutive castings can be combined to warp or unwarp an object too large for one spell, and the object suffers no ill effects until it is completely warped.

warp-wood.notes: Same as warp metal: the -4 belongs to the ruined weapon, not to a creature this spell targets.

effects.target: The target animal gains the combat training general purpose from the Handle Animal skill. This supersedes the animal's previous trained purpose and every trick it knows; when the spell ends it reverts to its previous purpose and tricks.

wartrain-mount.notes: Animal training has no effect type.

effects.target: You place a scrying sensor on your animal companion or familiar, letting it function as an insect summoned by greater insect spy. It does not change shape and does not lose the ability to make its own decisions, but it receives orders and gives answers as those insects do, and you can sense its direction and distance and receive sensory input from it.

watchful-animal.notes: Scrying has no home in the effect vocabulary.

effects.target: Functions as shield other, except that you must maintain line of effect to the target.

watchful-eye.notes: shield other's damage transfer and its +1 AC and saves are not restated in this description, so no numbers are emitted.

effects.target: Breathe water freely. The spell does not make you unable to breathe air.

water-breathing.notes: The duration is divided evenly among all the creatures touched, which the duration shape cannot express; the per-creature share is the emitted duration divided by the number touched.

effects.target: A spout of rushing water surrounds you, deflecting attacks. You take half damage from acid and fire-based attacks, and if such an attack allows a Reflex save for half damage you take none at all on a success. Any creature that strikes you with its body or a handheld weapon deals normal damage but immediately takes 1d6 points of acid damage + 1 point per 2 caster levels (maximum +10); the attacker's spell resistance applies to this. Creatures wielding weapons with exceptional reach are not subject to it.

water-shield.notes: The 1d6 + 1 per 2 levels is retributive — it lands on whoever attacks you, not on a target you choose — so it is not emitted as damage. This is the thorn body defect exactly. The acid and fire protection is 'half damage', not a flat point value, and the resistance type takes an integer amount, so it cannot be emitted either.

effects.target: Tread on any liquid as if it were firm ground — mud, oil, snow, quicksand, running water, ice, even lava — walking, running, charging or otherwise moving across the surface as if it were normal ground, with your feet hovering an inch or two above it. Crossing molten lava still means taking damage from the heat of being near it.
If the spell is cast underwater, or while the subjects are partly or wholly submerged, they are borne toward the surface at 60 feet per round until they can stand on it.

water-walk.notes: The heat damage near lava is environmental and unquantified here, so nothing is emitted for it.

effects.target: Tread on any liquid as if it were firm ground, as water walk.
You divide the duration in 10-minute intervals among the creatures touched.

water-walk-communal.notes: The emitted duration is the whole pool; each creature's share is whatever part of it you allot in 10-minute intervals, which the duration shape cannot express.

effects.target: The touched object, no larger than 10 pounds per caster level, becomes waterproof, protected from any mundane liquid such as alcohol or oil but not from magically created liquids. Cast on a creature, it waterproofs all of that creature's equipment for as long as the creature carries it; an item dropped or discarded loses the protection permanently, even if the target picks it up again. Mundane combustibles still need exposure to air to ignite.

waterproof.notes: Protection from mundane liquid is not damage resistance and has no effect type.

effects.target: Creates roughly 2 ounces of what appears to be clear pure water but is a foul secretion that functions in every way as unholy water. That is one dose, or one use as a thrown weapon if bottled. It can be stored indefinitely but cannot be created inside a creature. Extensive exposure — drinking nothing else for months — can bring on monstrous deformities or even total transformation into a beast at the GM's discretion, and these mutations are rarely if ever beneficial.
fort
effects.note: Any creature anointed with or drinking the fluid saves. A creature that drinks it takes a -4 penalty on the save.

on_failure.target: int
on_failure.note: The water wreaks havoc on the victim's mind. Intelligence cannot drop below 1 from this effect.

on_failure.target: dex
on_failure.note: The water twists and deforms the victim's body. Dexterity cannot drop below 1 from this effect.

on_success.note: The creature becomes violently ill and vomits up the fluid; sickened for 1d4 rounds. The duration is rolled, which the duration shape cannot hold.

waters-of-lamashtu.notes: The ability damage lands on the creature exposed to the fluid, which the spell's own 'Fortitude partial' entry treats as the subject, so it is emitted. Note that in play the exposure can come later, when the stored dose is drunk or thrown.

effects.target: A rushing torrent of water in the rough outline of a shield protects you from one physical or fire attack, granting you DR/- and fire resistance each equal to half your caster level (minimum 1) against that single attack. Once the spell has reduced the damage of one attack against you, it is discharged.

wave-shield.notes: VOCABULARY GAP: damage_reduction and resistance both take an integer amount, and this spell's amount is 'half your caster level (minimum 1)' — a formula. Emitting any fixed number would be wrong at every level but one, so both stay narrative. Corpus duration is 'rounds (1) or until discharged'.

effects.target: Torrents of roiling blood attempt a bull rush against every creature in the cone, regardless of size. Make a single combat maneuver check and apply the result to each creature; your CMB for it equals your caster level plus your Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma modifier, whichever is highest. This bull rush does not provoke attacks of opportunity.
fort
effects.note: Every creature in the area saves against the tide of blood.

on_failure.target: sickened
on_failure.note: For 1d6 rounds. The duration is rolled, which the duration shape cannot hold.

effects.target: The area covered by the cone stays slick for 1 round, so any creature trying to move within it must succeed at a DC 10 Acrobatics check as if moving on uneven ground. A creature that falls prone from failing that check must succeed at a Fortitude save or be sickened until it stands back up.

waves-of-blood.notes: Corpus duration is 'instantaneous and rounds (1) (see text)'; the 1 round is the slick ground left behind, and that is what the emitted duration times. The second Fortitude save happens only if a creature later falls prone, so it is described rather than gated.

effects.target: will
effects.note: Will partial; every creature in the 30-foot cone.

on_failure.target: stunned
staggered
on_failure.note: For the remainder of the spell's duration, after the first round of being stunned.

on_success.note: Staggered for the first round only; the creature can act normally thereafter.

waves-of-ecstasy.notes: A genuine partial save: failure is stunned then staggered, success is staggered for one round only, and both branches are emitted.

effects.target: exhausted
effects.note: All living creatures in the 60-foot cone; no saving throw is allowed. The spell has no effect on a creature that is already exhausted.

waves-of-exhaustion.notes: No save and no scaling — the prose is one sentence and it is entirely executable.

effects.target: fatigued
effects.note: All living creatures in the 30-foot cone; no saving throw is allowed. The spell has no effect on a creature that is already fatigued.

waves-of-fatigue.notes: One sentence of prose, entirely executable.

effects.target: damage
effects.note: Taken by whoever fires the altered ammunition from the target firearm.

effects.target: The target firearm's range increment is halved while it fires the altered ammunition. A user who is aware of the spell's effect before firing — a DC 16 Spellcraft check to identify the spell as it is cast, or a similar effect — can spend a standard action to clear the altered ammunition from the firearm, destroying that ammunition.

weaken-powder.notes: The -2 is emitted as a real modifier because this spell is about one firearm and the creature firing it, unlike warp metal where the weapon penalty is one item on a list of ways an arbitrary object can be ruined. The halved range increment is a multiplier, not an additive modifier, so it has no spec. The penalty has no stated bonus type.

effects.target: damage
effects.note: On damage rolls with the transformed weapon. A ranged weapon applies this to its ammunition.

effects.target: If the weapon scores a critical hit, the target of that critical hit becomes shaken for 1 round with no saving throw. This is a mind-affecting fear effect. You cannot cast this spell on a natural weapon, but you can cast it on an unarmed strike.

weapon-of-awe.notes: The shaken is deliberately not an apply_condition: the spell's target is the weapon, so an apply_condition would shake the wielder at cast time, when in fact it lands on whoever is later struck by a critical hit.

effects.target: Each affected weapon shines with pale light that dimly illuminates a 5-foot square, and ignores the damage reduction of evil creatures whose DR is 5 or lower, so long as that damage reduction is not DR/epic.

weapons-against-evil.notes: Ignoring someone else's damage reduction is the opposite direction from the damage_reduction type, which grants DR; there is no spec for bypassing it.

effects.target: Part of the weapon opens like a partly peeled apple, revealing a space for a single wand, which you may insert as part of casting; the weapon then closes around it with no harm to its integrity. For the duration, whoever wields the weapon counts as wielding the wand as well, and can attack normally with the weapon or use it as if it were the encased wand. If the wand's effect requires an attack roll, you may make that roll as an attack with the weapon at its highest bonus, including any bonuses the weapon would normally receive — this does not add the weapon's damage to the wand's effect, it only lends your skill with the weapon to the chance of hitting. When the duration ends the wand is ejected; you may catch it as a free action if you have a hand free, otherwise it drops to the ground. If the weapon housing the wand is broken or destroyed during the duration, the wand is broken or destroyed with it.

weaponwand.notes: Item combination has no effect type.

effects.target: ref
effects.note: The spell has no effect at all if the target is not on or adjacent to a solid surface that can support the webbing.

on_failure.target: The target is affected as if by a web spell occupying only its own space.

on_success.target: The remaining webs dissolve and the square does not count as difficult terrain. The same happens once a caught creature breaks free.

web-bolt.notes: The prose defers entirely to web for what being caught means and never restates it, so nothing is emitted for the entangling itself.

effects.target: A cloud of flame-resistant adhesive webbing billows and flows much as cloudkill does, moving away from you at 10 feet per round and rolling along the ground; each round work out its new spread from a point of origin 10 feet farther from where you cast it. Being heavier than air it sinks to the lowest ground, even pouring down dens and sinkholes, cannot penetrate liquids and cannot be cast underwater. A creature in the cloud at the start of its turn must save against it or be affected; it otherwise acts as a web spell. Creatures trapped in the webbing stay trapped after the cloud passes, but the area it leaves behind does not count as difficult terrain. The webbing is flammable as web is, but has fire resistance 5.

web-cloud.notes: The Reflex save happens at the start of each creature's turn inside a cloud that moves on its own, not at casting, so no save_gate is emitted. The fire resistance 5 belongs to the webbing, not to a creature, so it is not a resistance spec.

effects.target: You create a shelter of slightly sticky webbing with a hinged door large enough for a Medium creature. Its opaque walls are 1 inch thick and give total cover to anyone inside. Only Fine creatures with negligible Strength, including swarms, can be caught in the webbing; every other creature pulls free without a Strength check and without spending an action. The webbing holds twigs, leaves, dirt and other light items, so the shelter can be concealed, and it is watertight and insulated with the door closed. Its surface has hardness 0 and 2 hit points per 5-foot square of web surface, takes normal damage from fire and burns as easily as wood. When the spell ends the webbing decays rapidly and disappears.

web-shelter.notes: A created structure; the total cover it gives is a property of the shelter rather than a modifier on a creature.

effects.target: will

While the spell lasts your mind-affecting spells carry a supernatural taint. Whenever you successfully affect a creature with one of them — the target failing its save, or the spell allowing none — that target must also succeed at a Fortitude save against what grows within or be afflicted by a lesser seeded infestation. Lesser seeded infestation: save Fortitude at this spell's save DC; onset immediate; frequency 1/day; effect 1d4 Constitution drain; cure none, curable by magic alone. A creature whose Constitution is reduced to 0 by it dies and rises 1d4 rounds later as a seeded creature. Each creature so afflicted reduces this spell's remaining duration by 1 round, and if you affect several in a round you choose the order in which they save. The infestation does not expose its victim to Xhamen-Dor's infectious dreams. Preparing this spell for the first time, or first using it from a spell-completion or spell-trigger item, makes you a possible target of Xhamen-Dor's infected dreams ability thereafter.

what-grows-within.notes: The +3 profane on Will saves is the only thing that happens to you at casting and is emitted. The 1d4 Constitution drain lands on a third party — a creature your later mind-affecting spells affect — and recurs daily, so it is not an ability_drain spec.

effects.target: Wield a whip of hundreds of Diminutive spiders sized for you, attacking with it as a whip except that you make a melee touch attack instead of a regular attack. Any creature you strike takes swarm damage as if attacked by a spider swarm — 1d6 points of damage plus poison and distraction. The swarm whip can damage creatures with armour or natural armour where a normal whip could not, but cannot make bull rush, grapple or trip attacks, and unlike a swarm it is subject to miss chances for concealment and cover.

The whip is immune to all weapon damage, is never staggered or reduced to a dying state by damage, and is immune to any spell or effect that targets a specific number of creatures, including single-target spells such as disintegrate. It takes half again as much damage from area spells and effects, but counts as part of your gear, so it takes damage only when you fail a saving throw on a natural 1 or when an opponent specifically targets it. It has none of a swarm's vulnerability to high winds. As a standard action you can transform the whip into a spider swarm, all of whose squares must be within 15 feet of you, after which it functions as summon swarm; that swarm has 3 hit points and lasts 2 rounds or until this spell ends, whichever comes first.

whip-of-spiders.notes: The 1d6 is dealt by an attack the spell grants, on a later melee touch attack, so it is not emitted as damage — the brief's exclusion for granted natural attacks covers it exactly. The 3 hit points belong to the summoned swarm.

effects.target: Wield a whip of army ants, as whip of spiders, attacking with a melee touch attack. Any creature you strike takes swarm damage as if attacked by an army ant swarm — 3d6 points of damage plus poison and distraction.
As whip of spiders in all other respects, except that transforming the whip into an army ant swarm gives that swarm 16 hit points.

whip-of-ants.notes: The 3d6 is the army ant swarm's damage, dealt by an attack the spell grants on a later touch attack, so it is not a damage spec.

effects.target: Wield a whip of centipedes, as whip of spiders, attacking with a melee touch attack. Any creature you strike takes swarm damage as if attacked by a centipede swarm — 2d6 points of damage plus poison and distraction.
As whip of spiders in all other respects, except that transforming the whip into a centipede swarm gives that swarm 10 hit points.

whip-of-centipedes.notes: The 2d6 is the centipede swarm's damage, dealt by an attack the spell grants on a later touch attack, so it is not a damage spec.

effects.target: A powerful cyclone of raging wind moves through the air, along the ground or over water at 60 feet per round. You may concentrate on its every movement or give it a simple program; directing it or changing that program is a standard action, and it always moves during your turn. If it leaves the spell's range it moves randomly and uncontrolled for 1d3 rounds and then dissipates, and you cannot regain control of it even if it returns within range.
