effects.note: Any Large or smaller creature that comes in contact with the cyclone saves.

on_failure.note: The prose states no damage type for this.

effects.target: A Medium or smaller creature that fails that first save must succeed at a second or be picked up bodily and held suspended in the winds, taking 1d8 points of damage each round on your turn with no save allowed. You may direct the cyclone to eject any creature it carries whenever you wish, dropping it wherever the cyclone happens to be.

whirlwind.notes: Same shape as vortex: the 3d6 on contact is one hit on the creature that touched it and is emitted; the 1d8 repeats every round with no save and stays narrative. Unlike vortex the prose names no damage type, so untyped is recorded rather than borrowing vortex's bludgeoning.

effects.target: Knowledge checks of the single type appropriate to the terrain you are currently in

Cold, desert, forest, jungle, mountain, plains, swamp and water environments give the bonus on Knowledge (nature); underground gives it on Knowledge (dungeoneering); urban gives it on Knowledge (local); any plane other than the Material Plane gives it on Knowledge (planes). Entering new terrain loses the old bonus and gains the new one.

whispering-lore.notes: Emitted as a situational_mod rather than four skill_mod specs: which Knowledge skill it applies to changes with the terrain and changes again as you walk, so four skill_mods would grant all four bonuses at once.

effects.target: You send a message or sound on the wind to a specific location within range that is familiar to you, provided the wind can find a way there. It travels as gently and unnoticed as a zephyr, then delivers its whisper-quiet message or sound whether or not anyone is present to hear it, and dissipates. You may give it a message of no more than 25 words, have it deliver other sounds for 1 round, or have it seem merely a faint stirring of the air, and you may set its speed anywhere from 1 mile per hour to 1 mile per 10 minutes. On reaching its objective it swirls and remains in place until the message is delivered. As with magic mouth, it cannot speak verbal components, use command words or activate magical effects.

whispering-wind.notes: Message delivery has no effect type. Corpus duration is 'hours/level (1) or until discharged'; delivering the message is the discharge.

effects.target: Reeds, grasses, creepers or thin tree branches you touch animate into a wicker horse complete with riding saddle, keeping a wickerlike appearance. It has the statistics of a light horse or a pony, except that it gains construct traits and counts as both an animal and a construct for spells and effects, and gains extra hit points equal to your caster level. It has no skills or feats except these: reeds give Swim ranks equal to your caster level; grasses give the Run feat and Acrobatics ranks equal to your caster level; creepers give ranks in Climb and Stealth equal to your caster level; tree branches leave it continually affected by barkskin at your caster level. It obeys no Handle Animal commands and only you can ride it. You can cast this spell only where suitable plant material is available. When the spell ends or the horse loses all its hit points, it falls apart.

wicker-horse.notes: All the numbers belong to the animated horse, not to the caster.

effects.target: The range of your antipaladin or paladin auras doubles — a paladin's aura of courage, for instance, affects allies within 20 feet instead of 10.

widen-auras.notes: Doubling the radius of an existing class feature is not something the vocabulary can express; the 20 feet in the prose is a worked example of the doubling, not a number this spell sets.

effects.target: Perception checks to act in a surprise round
You become aware of sounds and smells you would normally overlook, and take no penalty on Perception checks while sleeping.
Choose to wake if you notice a threat while asleep.

wild-instinct.notes: The sleeping clause says only 'you don't take a penalty' and never names the number, so unlike vigilant rest — which states the +10 outright — no modifier is emitted for it. The +5 has no stated bonus type.

effects.target: Nearby plants fight for you; the spell does nothing if no plants you can direct are within the area. On each of your turns you may spend a swift action and/or a standard action to direct one attack. The attack bonus or CMB for these attacks equals your base attack bonus + your Wisdom modifier, and the spell grants a +1 bonus per 3 caster levels (maximum +5) on their damage rolls. Your wilderness soldiers never provoke attacks of opportunity and do not count as allies for flanking or any other purpose. Tree: a melee attack with 10-foot reach from its trunk dealing 1d8 points of damage + your Wisdom modifier, or instead a bull rush, drag or reposition combat maneuver at the same reach; the tree cannot move itself. Undergrowth or hedgerow: acting as a Medium creature, one square attempts a grapple against an opponent within or adjacent to it, heavy undergrowth gaining +2 to its CMD. It cannot move the grapple or pin a foe, but a successful grapple check against a foe it holds deals 1d4 points of damage + your Wisdom modifier. Its CMD is 5 + its CMB, and it releases its opponent if you do not direct it to maintain the grapple.

wilderness-soldiers.notes: The 1d8 and 1d4 are dealt by the plants the spell animates, on attacks you direct on later turns, so neither is a damage spec. The +1 per 3 levels applies to those plants' damage rolls, not yours, so it is deliberately not a combat_mod — that would add it to the caster's own weapon damage.

effects.target: fly
effects.note: Perfect maneuverability. If the subject wishes, a magical wind instead wafts it along at up to 600 feet per round (60 mph) with poor maneuverability.

effects.target: You and the creatures you touch become cloudlike vapor as gaseous form and move through the air, each acting independently. Wind walkers are not invisible but appear misty and translucent, and one fully clothed in white is 80% likely to be mistaken for cloud, fog or vapor. A wind walker can regain its physical form at will and later resume cloud form; each change takes 5 rounds, which counts against the spell's duration, as does any time spent in physical form. For the last minute of the duration a wind walker in cloud form automatically descends 60 feet per round, 600 feet in all, though it may descend faster — this descent is the warning that the spell is about to end.

wind-walk.notes: The only spell in this partition whose prose states it is dismissible, and it can be dismissed for individual wind walkers and not others — which the duration flag cannot express. The 10-foot fly speed is stated plainly and is emitted; the 600-feet-per-round option is the subject's alternative, recorded on the same spec rather than as a second speed.

effects.target: An invisible vertical curtain of wind 2 feet thick and of considerable strength — a roaring blast that blows away any bird smaller than an eagle and tears papers and similar materials from unsuspecting hands, though a Reflex save lets a creature keep hold of an object. Tiny and Small flying creatures cannot pass through it. Loose materials and cloth garments caught in it fly upward. Arrows and bolts are deflected upward and miss, and any other normal ranged weapon passing through has a 30% miss chance, though giant-thrown boulders, siege engine projectiles and other massive ranged weapons are unaffected. Gases, most gaseous breath weapons and creatures in gaseous form cannot pass it, but it is no barrier to incorporeal creatures. It must be vertical, but you can shape it in any continuous path along the ground, including cylinders or squares that enclose a point.

wind-wall.notes: Miss chances and movement barriers have no effect type; the Reflex save is only to keep hold of an object, not against an effect the vocabulary can name.

effects.note: Against the single attack you respond to by becoming vaporous.

effects.target: poison, sneak attack and critical hit effects from the attack you respond to
You cannot use windy escape against an attack of opportunity you provoked by casting a spell, using a spell-like ability, or using any other magical ability that provokes when used.

windy-escape.notes: Both the DR and the immunity are stated flatly and apply to exactly one attack, which the once-only use limit carries.

effects.target: Your wings sprout colourful, flavourful berries, each functioning as if affected by goodberry. You may choose for one of them to be poisonous instead, as striped toadstool; only you and druids of 5th level or higher can tell which is which without magic.

wing-bounty.notes: goodberry's healing and the toadstool's poison are both deferred to by name and never restated here, so no numbers are emitted.

effects.target: Use the poisonous thorns on your wings like armour spikes, and make two wing attacks as primary natural weapons. If you are Small the wings deal 1d3 points of bludgeoning and piercing damage plus your Strength modifier — or count as secondary natural weapons if you also attack with a weapon.
A creature damaged by your wing thorns experiences intense itching and gains the sickened condition for as long as the spell lasts, unless it succeeds at a Fortitude saving throw.

wing-thorns.notes: The 1d3 is a natural attack the spell grants, which the brief excludes from damage specs outright. The sickened lands on a creature your wings later damage, after its own Fortitude save, so it is not an apply_condition — that would sicken the caster at cast time. The prose gives damage only for a Small caster and never states the Medium figure; nothing is invented to fill that in.

effects.target: The targeted melee weapon grows small feathered wings and acts as if it had the throwing weapon special ability. This spell can stand in for magic stone as a prerequisite for the throwing weapon special ability.

winged-sword.notes: Weapon special abilities have no effect type; the spell states no bonus of its own.

effects.target: harm from cold environments down to -50 degrees Fahrenheit, and the Fortitude saves such conditions require
effects.note: The target's equipment is protected as well.

effects.target: Stealth checks to hide in ice and snow, if you chose at casting to turn the target's feathers white
This gives no protection from cold damage, nor from other environmental hazards of cold weather such as slipping on ice or snow blindness.

winter-feathers.notes: The white feathers are optional at casting, so the +4 is a situational_mod — which the GM reads and applies — rather than a skill_mod the engine would grant every casting whether or not the caster chose it. The prose is explicit that this is environmental protection and not cold resistance, so no resistance spec is emitted.

effects.target: By speaking aloud you alter reality, producing any one of these effects. Duplicate any sorcerer/wizard spell of 8th level or lower, or any non-sorcerer/wizard spell of 7th level or lower, provided it is not from one of your opposition schools; or any sorcerer/wizard spell of 7th level or lower, or non-sorcerer/wizard spell of 6th level or lower, even from an opposition school. Undo the harmful effects of many other spells, such as geas/quest or insanity. Grant a creature a +1 inherent bonus to an ability score — two to five wishes cast in immediate succession grant +2 to +5, inherent bonuses are instantaneous and cannot be dispelled, may never exceed +5 for one score, and do not stack, so only the best applies. Remove injuries and afflictions, aiding one creature per caster level, all cured of the same kind of affliction — heal all the damage you and your companions have taken, or remove all poison from everyone in the party, but not both with one wish. Revive the dead by duplicating resurrection; reviving a creature whose body was destroyed takes two wishes, one to recreate the body and one to infuse it with life, and no wish prevents the permanent negative level. Transport travellers, lifting one creature per caster level from anywhere on any plane to anywhere else on any plane regardless of local conditions, an unwilling target getting a Will save and spell resistance. Undo misfortune, forcing a reroll of any roll made within the last round including your last turn — an opponent's successful save, a foe's successful critical hit or its confirmation, a friend's failed save — though the reroll may be as bad or worse, and an unwilling target gets a Will save and spell resistance. Attempting greater effects is dangerous: the wish may pervert your intent into a literal but undesirable fulfilment, or fulfil it only partly, at the GM's discretion. Duplicated spells allow saves and spell resistance as normal, but their save DCs are those of a 9th-level spell, and duplicating a spell with a material component costing more than 10,000 gp means providing that component too, on top of this spell's 25,000 gp diamond.

wish.notes: A menu of nine alternatives, exactly one of which happens per casting; any spec emitted would be the wrong one eight times out of nine. Corpus duration is 'see text' and the prose states none, so duration is omitted.

effects.target: being checked or blown away by winds of less than windstorm force
effects.note: The target can still choose to be moved by such winds if it wishes.

with-the-wind.notes: One clause of prose and it fits the immunity type cleanly.

effects.target: You push your hand into the subject and withdraw an affliction from its body as a tangible object, a slimy mass of flesh. The target is cured as if by remove disease, remove curse or neutralize poison. The slimy mass then lets you deliver that affliction to another creature with a touch attack, as if holding the charge for a touch spell, with the same effect, saving throw and DC as the original affliction.

withdraw-affliction.notes: VOCABULARY GAP: the condition vocabulary has no diseased, cursed or poisoned entry, so remove_condition cannot express curing an affliction — the whole spell is about afflictions the vocabulary cannot name. Transferring the affliction to a new victim has no type either.

effects.target: Shift your senses from yourself to the target or back as a move action. While using the target's senses you are blind and deaf, and you perceive with its normal and special senses — its darkvision, for instance — rather than your own.
You link your senses to a living target, seeing and hearing through its eyes and ears.

witness.notes: The sense type names specific senses a creature gains, not a link to another creature's senses, so the link itself is a permission.

effects.target: The target appears to be an older version of itself, by however much you select — '10 years older', 'as an adult'. You cannot change its appearance in any way not directly associated with ageing, though hair may grey and liver spots appear. Children of creatures that are Medium or smaller when fully grown may grow one size category to the normal adult size for their kind; otherwise the age increase does not alter size, and a change in size does not alter ability scores. The spell causes no age-based modifications to ability scores and no other age-related effects such as dragon age categories or natural metamorphoses. Wizened appearance and youthful appearance counter and dispel each other.

wizened-appearance.notes: Not gated on the Fortitude save, for the same reason as vocal alteration: it is normally cast on a willing subject for disguise, and gating would make it fail to work on that subject. The prose says outright that ability scores do not change, so nothing is emitted.

effects.target: You form one existing piece of wood — no larger than 10 cubic feet plus 1 cubic foot per caster level — into any shape that suits your purpose. Crude coffers, doors and the like are possible but fine detail is not, and any shape that includes moving parts has a 30% chance of simply not working.

wood-shape.notes: Shaping matter has no effect type.

effects.target: You create 1d4+2 wood golems with the advanced template. They willingly aid you in combat, perform a specific mission, or serve as bodyguards. You can have only one wooden phalanx in effect at a time; casting it again while an earlier casting persists dispels the earlier one.

wooden-phalanx.notes: Summoning has no effect type, and 1d4+2 is a count of golems, not damage or healing dice, so it does not belong in scaling.

effects.target: ac
effects.note: Your wings become a wooden barrier resembling a tower shield. If you move, the spell ends immediately.

wooden-wing-shield.notes: Corpus duration is 'rounds/level (1) or until you move'; the movement clause cannot be expressed by the duration shape and is recorded on the spec.

effects.target: You inscribe a rune on any surface. It triggers when any non-plant creature other than you moves within 30 feet of it. In all other respects the spell functions as symbol of death.
fort
effects.note: Every creature caught in the 30-foot burst when the rune triggers. Plant creatures and creatures under woodland stride or freedom of movement are not affected at all.

on_failure.target: Roots and branches sprout from the ground and hinder the creature's movement as if it were moving through heavy undergrowth. They give no concealment.

woodland-rune.notes: The prose says movement is hindered 'as if moving through heavy undergrowth', which is difficult terrain rather than the entangled condition, so no apply_condition is emitted — entangled would also impose a Dexterity penalty and an attack penalty the spell never mentions. Corpus duration is 'permanent until discharged'.

effects.target: Functions as sending, except that the subject also learns a command word which, if spoken within 1 round of learning it, summons you to the open space nearest the subject. The subject is not obliged to speak it. You can be transported any distance within a plane but never between planes, and may bring objects up to your maximum load, plus one additional willing Medium or smaller creature — carrying gear up to its own maximum load — or its equivalent per 3 caster levels, a Large creature counting as two Medium, a Huge as four and so on. Every creature transported must be in contact with the others, and at least one of them in contact with you.
will
effects.note: Only nonchaotic creatures in the 40-foot-radius spread are affected, and creatures whose Hit Dice exceed your caster level are unaffected entirely. A creature subject to several of the effects below makes only one save and applies the result to all of them.

on_failure.target: The effects are cumulative and concurrent, by the creature's Hit Dice compared to your caster level. Hit Dice equal to your caster level: deafened for 1d4 rounds. Up to caster level -1: stunned for 1 round, and deafened. Up to caster level -5: confused for 1d10 minutes (a mind-affecting enchantment effect), stunned and deafened. Up to caster level -10: killed — living creatures die and undead are destroyed — as well as confused, stunned and deafened.

on_success.target: The save negates the deafness, the stunning and the death, and reduces the confusion to 1 round. A creature in the lowest Hit Dice band, which would have been killed, instead takes 3d6 points of damage + 1 point per caster level (maximum +25) on a successful save.

effects.target: If you are on your home plane when you cast this spell, nonchaotic extraplanar creatures in the area are instantly banished to their home planes and cannot return for at least 24 hours. This happens whether or not they hear the word, and allows a separate Will save at a -4 penalty to negate.

word-of-chaos.notes: The 3d6 + 1 per caster level is deliberately not a damage spec and gets no scaling entry: it is dealt only on a SUCCESSFUL save, and only to creatures in the lowest Hit Dice band. Reading it as the spell's damage would deal it to everyone on a failed save — the inverse of the rule. Which band a creature falls into depends on its Hit Dice against your caster level, which cannot be known at conversion time, so the whole table stays narrative. Corpus duration is instantaneous. The corpus already derives element 'sonic'.

effects.target: You are teleported instantly back to a sanctuary you designated when you prepared the spell, which must be a very familiar place; the arrival point is a designated area no larger than 10 feet by 10 feet. You can travel any distance within a plane but never between planes, and may bring any objects you carry up to your maximum load, plus one additional willing Medium or smaller creature — carrying gear up to its own maximum load — or its equivalent per 3 caster levels, a Large creature counting as two Medium and a Huge as two Large. All creatures transported must be in contact with one another and at least one in contact with you; exceeding the limit makes the spell fail. An unwilling creature cannot be teleported, and a creature's Will save or spell resistance stops items in its possession from being teleported. Unattended nonmagical objects get no save.
The target ally immediately rerolls one failed saving throw against a charm or fear effect.
the rerolled saving throw against a charm or fear effect

If you do not have the aura of courage class ability, this spell has no effect on the target's fear. If you do not have the aura of resolve class ability, it has no effect on any charm effects on the target.

word-of-resolve.notes: The prose never names which saving throw a charm or fear effect calls for, so the +4 is a situational_mod against the reroll rather than a save_mod against a guessed Will.

effects.target: Natural terrain surges beneath you and carries you across great distances. Choose the wave's type at casting: a tsunami, a 30-foot-high tidal wave of earth or water lasting 1 round per level, or a swell, a controlled 5-foot-high wave lasting 1 hour per level. Either way the crest extends 10 feet in front of and behind you and 5 feet per level to each side, moves at eight times your base land speed, and you may stand, sit, lie down, sleep or take any action on it that you could take on solid ground. You may grant up to one additional creature per level the ability to ride it safely. You choose its path by facing a direction when you create it and can never change that decision, nor alter the wave's dimensions. Anything strongly connected to or part of the natural world simply rises and falls with the wave unharmed; anything else that contacts it takes 6d6 points of bludgeoning damage from a tsunami or 1d6 from a swell. The wave damages any manufactured object or structure, and on the Material Plane any aberration, construct, outsider or undead creature or creature with the extraplanar subtype — constructs and undead taking double damage. Any other creature, and any creature with even one druid class level whatever its type, is part of the natural world and unaffected; on other planes what counts as natural is the GM's call. The wave can climb or descend natural features up to a 45-degree angle. Terrain it cannot incorporate — anything primarily of fire such as lava, of air such as an open cliff face, or man-made such as a city — is flowed over or around, riders being harmlessly displaced sideways, unless that terrain fills half or more of the crest, in which case the spell ends in 1d6 rounds as the wave falters and collapses, its momentum carrying you on unharmed until it does, whereupon you suffer the normal effects of the terrain you are deposited in. You can create the wave only while standing on the ground, never underground or on terrain it cannot incorporate.

world-wave.notes: The 6d6 and 1d6 belong to two mutually exclusive versions chosen at casting, land on whatever later contacts a moving wave rather than on a target at cast time, and apply only to particular creature types while sparing everything else — three separate reasons not to emit them as damage. Duration is omitted for the same reason: the corpus says 'rounds/level (1) or hours/level (1)', which are the tsunami and the swell, and the shape cannot hold a choice between two.

effects.target: Make a ranged touch attack with a ray of sickly greenish-gray negative energy. A creature hit is wracked by painful spasms as its muscles and sinews wither.
fort
effects.note: Fortitude halves the ability damage.

on_failure.target: The subject takes 1d4 points of Dexterity damage and 1d4 points of Strength damage per 3 caster levels, to a maximum of 5d4 each. This spell cannot reduce an ability score below 1.

wracking-ray.notes: VOCABULARY GAP: the ability damage scales at 1d4 per 3 caster levels to a cap, and nothing can express that — `scaling` drives damage and healing dice only (no corpus spell scales an ability_damage spec), and one spell-level scaling entry could not drive two separate scores anyway. Emitting ability_damage with dice '1d4' would be right only up to caster level 5 and wrong at every level above, so both scores stay in a narrative spec with the formula intact. Corpus duration is instantaneous.

effects.target: attack
effects.note: Only against one enemy creature you can see and designate at casting. +1 per three caster levels, minimum +1, maximum +3.

effects.target: damage
effects.note: Weapon damage rolls against the designated creature only. +1 per three caster levels, minimum +1, maximum +3.

effects.target: spell_resistance
effects.note: Caster level checks made to overcome the designated creature's spell resistance. +1 per three caster levels, minimum +1, maximum +3.

effects.target: At 12th level you gain the benefits of the Improved Critical feat on attack rolls made against the designated creature. This does not stack with any other effect that expands a weapon's threat range.

wrath.notes: The base +1 is emitted, correct through caster level 5, with the per-three-levels progression to a maximum of +3 recorded on every spec — the same modifier-scaling gap as ward the faithful.

effects.target: You grant the touched melee weapon one of these weapon special abilities: anarchic, axiomatic, holy or unholy. The spell takes the matching descriptor — chaos for anarchic, law for axiomatic, good for holy, evil for unholy. If you try to place a special ability on a weapon that already has it, the spell fails. A warpriest casting this on his sacred weapon doubles the duration, and a warpriest whose sacred weapon is the unarmed strike can cast it on his unarmed strike.

wrathful-weapon.notes: Four mutually exclusive weapon special abilities, none of whose numbers this description states — it defers to the abilities by name. The warpriest duration doubling is a conditional the duration shape cannot hold.

effects.target: Functions as symbol of death, except that creatures which succumb become dominated by Hastur, as dominate monster. They seek to aid any obvious minion or worshiper of Hastur in sight, and any true worshiper of Hastur can command them as if that worshiper had dominated them; conflicting commands from different true worshipers are settled by opposed Charisma checks, the winner commanding the targets that round. With no worshiper or agent of Hastur in sight, an affected creature acts normally. The domination lasts 1 round per level, and once triggered the Yellow Sign itself remains active for 10 minutes per caster level. There is a 1% chance when a creature fails its save that Hastur takes note and decides to control the target personally: the dominated creature's actions are then the GM's to determine, the effects persist for 1 day per level, and no other creature can countermand the commands, not even a Hastur worshiper. However long the effects last, and whether or not Hastur controls the victim directly, any creature that failed to resist this spell can be targeted by Hastur's fulvous dreams ability for the rest of its life, should the Great Old One ever choose to. Yellow Sign can be made permanent with permanency by a caster of 18th level or higher for 40,000 gp.

yellow-sign.notes: Domination has no effect type, and the three different durations here (1 round/level for the domination, 10 minutes/caster level for the sign, 1 day/level if Hastur intervenes) are why the corpus duration reads 'see text'; no single duration would be true, so it is omitted.

effects.target: The target looks like a younger version of itself, by however much you select — '10 years', 'as a young adult'. You cannot change any detail of its appearance not directly associated with ageing, though grey hair returns to its original colour, and it cannot appear so much younger that its size changes. The spell does not affect any age-based modifications to ability scores or other age-related effects.

youthful-appearance.notes: The prose says explicitly that ability scores are untouched, so nothing is emitted. Counters and is countered by wizened appearance.

effects.target: land
effects.note: An enhancement bonus; the speed type has no bonus_type field.

effects.target: fly
effects.note: An enhancement bonus, and only if the target already has a fly speed — the spell grants no flight of its own.

effects.target: Move and charge through difficult terrain without penalty.

zephyr-s-fleetness.notes: The fly bonus is conditional on the target already having a fly speed, which the spec cannot express, so it is recorded in the note — applying +30 fly to a creature that cannot fly would invent a movement mode the spell never grants.

effects.target: saving throws against fire effects
effects.note: All creatures in the zone gain this, except a creature saving against fire damage from its own magic.

effects.target: The zone looks unremarkable, though a Perception check against DC 20 + the caster's level reveals a faint rippling in the air like heat distortion. Whenever a creature inside casts a spell with the fire descriptor or activates a magical fire effect, from a magic item or a special attack, that creature takes full fire damage from its own effect; if the effect allows a saving throw to reduce the damage, the creature may attempt that same save. Nonmagical fire in the zone burns half as brightly but is otherwise unaffected.

zone-of-foul-flames.notes: The backlash damage is retributive in the strictest sense — it is the victim's own fire effect turned on them, with an amount that depends entirely on whatever spell they cast — so there is no number here to emit and nothing that lands at cast time.

effects.target: You manipulate sound waves around you so that you and everyone within the 5-foot-radius emanation can converse normally while no one outside hears your voices or any other noise from within, including language-dependent and sonic spell effects. The zone is centred on you and moves with you; anyone entering it immediately becomes subject to it and anyone leaving is no longer affected. A successful DC 20 Linguistics check to read lips can still reveal what is said inside.

zone-of-silence.notes: Containing sound has no effect type; it is not the silence condition, since creatures inside can speak and cast normally.

effects.target: will
effects.note: Each potentially affected creature saves when the spell is cast, or when it first enters the emanation. Creatures who leave the area are free to speak as they choose.

on_failure.target: The creature cannot speak any deliberate and intentional lie while within the emanation. Affected creatures know they are enchanted, so they may refuse to answer questions they would normally lie about, or be evasive while staying within the bounds of the truth.

zone-of-truth.notes: Compelled honesty has no effect type; apply_condition has nothing close, so the compulsion is narrative inside a gate that does model the Will save correctly.
